english: Why, kind one, does the dawn redden? When the dawn reddens, it rains. My mother said this to me. Does it snow? It does not snow; the frost has gone.
uncertain: h₁rudʰéh₁ti vs h₁rudʰéh₁eti: two different stems of the same verb in adjacent sentences

english: Daughter, go to the spring and bring water. It is cold. Cold water is good in the heat. Now I am bringing a lot.
uncertain: bʰréh₁wr̥ read as 'spring/well' (bare accusative of goal)

english: Mother, has it grown light? It has not grown light. The dawn has not come. Lie down. Sleep (?). Son, cover yourself with the wool.
uncertain: stéwdm̥-ge: stem unclear to me; guessed 'sleep/rest'

english: What is frost? At night the ground ___ and at dawn frost covers the walls. Does the frost melt? It melts when the sun shines.
uncertain: stéwdt: verb sense unknown to me (maybe 'grows cold/stiff')

english: The snow is melting and I am going. Guest, be well. May the gods protect you. Give me ___; you are dear. Come back in the warm season.
uncertain: h₁uséwōm ... déh₃tor: object noun and verb form unclear

english: Sister, I am asking for this wool. Winter is coming. Spin (?) for me, you. I give you a ring. Is your house warm? Yes, warm. My husband sits by the fire.
